title.value: A portrait of the different configurations between digitally-enabled innovations and climate governance
title.justification: The title directly reflects the overarching theme of the paper, which is exploring the different ways digital innovations are influencing climate governance.
title.quote: A portrait of the different configurations between digitally-enabled innovations and climate governance

extractions.description: The paper explores how digital technologies are being leveraged to transform climate governance. It discusses the categorization of digitally-enabled initiatives into four strategies: data mobilization, optimization of existing strategies, incentivizing and automating behavioral change, and enhancing participation and empowerment. These strategies are analyzed through the lens of the Earth System Governance framework’s 5 A’s – Architecture, Agency, Adaptiveness, Accountability, and Allocation & Access, to understand their potential in re-imagining climate governance.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily discusses how digital technologies influence climate mitigation initiatives and governance, exploring several strategies for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and supporting sustainable practices.
primary_category.quote: This work provides a first step towards understanding how digitally-enabled initiatives are contributing to re-imagining climate governance.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper specifically mentions the importance of connectivity and digital solutions to address environmental management issues in the Global South, aiming at leveraging digital technologies to strengthen climate governance in these regions.
secondary_categories.quote: Indeed, such countries often lack resources and show fragile organization, thus hindering the transformative potential of their initiatives. Connectivity has been proposed as an effective tool to overcome these issues in environmental management.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper covers multiple aspects and strategies influencing climate governance through digital technologies, spanning several potential sub-categories without focusing on one specific application like renewable energy or transportation.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a categorization of four types of strategies: data mobilization, optimization of existing strategies, incentivizing and automating behavioural change, and enhancing participation and empowerment of individuals.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper emphasizes the need for sharing knowledge and utilizing digital innovations to empower better climate governance, which falls within the scope of policy advice and knowledge sharing.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Indeed, transdisciplinary collaborations (e.g. data sharing) are often sought out in environmental governance as environmental issues are complex and multifaceted.

applications.justification: The paper explores how digital technologies, like satellite imagery, AI, and blockchain, are used to influence climate governance, illustrating practical applications of these technologies in policy and decision-making processes.
applications.quote: By using statistical models and algorithms to analyse data, including large datasets such as big data, machine learning helps to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in various ways including through better forecasting, prediction, and efficiency gains.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper fits well into the existing category of Climate Change Mitigation, focusing on governance and policy leveraging digital technologies.
new_primary_category.quote: There is a proliferation of climate action leveraging digital technologies that have emerged over the past decade.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: While the paper spans multiple strategies and doesn’t focus on a singular sub-category, it does not necessitate the creation of a new sub-category given the broad applicability across existing ones.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Initiatives were reviewed and grouped under one of the four strategies that most aligned with the approach adopted to influence climate governance.
